name: Melle Mel
hook: Took a song his own group did not want to make and delivered it in a voice that changed what rap was allowed to be about.
blurb: Melle Mel rapped with Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five, who were built for parties. When Sugar Hill's Sylvia Robinson pushed 'The Message' at them in 1982, the group did not want it: it was slow, it was grim, and it would not work in a club. Mel wrote verses for it anyway, by his own account without much enthusiasm at first. His delivery on it, heavy and deliberate and closer to preaching than partying, is why the record lands, and after it rap could be about anything. Two facts sit side by side here. The artistic breakthrough is truly his. And the song, written by someone else about conditions his group had no business reason to describe, only exists because a label boss overruled the group's own judgement.
